protocolGetter = llvm.externalFunction(protocolGetterProto)\n\n        // a protocol getter can call objc_retain, which takes a global objc lock see KT-80770\n        functionGenerationContext.switchThreadState(ThreadState.Native)\n        val result = call(protocolGetter, emptyList())\n        functionGenerationContext.switchThreadState(ThreadState.Runnable)\n        return result\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n    private val kTrue = llvm.int1(true)\n    private val kFalse = llvm.int1(false)\n\n    // TODO: Intrinsify?\n    private fun evaluateOperatorCall(callee: IrCall, args: List<LLVMValueRef>): LLVMValueRef {\n        context.log{\"evaluateOperatorCall           : origin:${ir2string(callee)}\"}\n        val function = callee.symbol.owner\n        val ib = context.irBuiltIns\n\n        with(functionGenerationContext) {\n            val functionSymbol = function.symbol\n            return when (functionSymbol) {\n                ib.eqeqeqSymbol -> icmpEq(args[0], args[1])\n                ib.booleanNotSymbol -> icmpNe(args[0], kTrue)\n                else -> {\n                    val isFloatingPoint = args[0].type.isFloatingPoint()\n                    // LLVM does not distinguish between signed/unsigned integers, so we must check\n                    // the parameter type.\n                    val shouldUseUnsignedComparison = function.parameters[0].type.isChar()\n                    when {\n                        functionSymbol.isComparisonFunction(ib.greaterFunByOperandType) -> {\n                            when {\n                                isFloatingPoint -> fcmpGt(args[0], args[1])\n                                shouldUseUnsignedComparison -> icmpUGt(args[0], args[1])\n                                else -> icmpGt(args[0], args[1])\n                            }\n                        }\n                        functionSymbol.isComparisonFunction(ib.greaterOrEqualFunByOperandType) -> {\n                            when {\n                                isFloatingPoint -> fcmpGe(args[0], args[1])\n                                shouldUseUnsignedComparison -> icmpUGe(args[0], args[1])\n                                else -> icmpGe(args[0], args[1])\n                            }\n                        }\n                        functionSymbol.isComparisonFunction(ib.lessFunByOperandType) -> {\n                            when {\n                                isFloatingPoint -> fcmpLt(args[0], args[1])\n                                shouldUseUnsignedComparison -> icmpULt(args[0], args[1])\n                                else -> icmpLt(args[0], args[1])\n                            }\n                        }\n                        functionSymbol.isComparisonFunction(ib.lessOrEqualFunByOperandType) -> {\n                            when {\n                                isFloatingPoint -> fcmpLe(args[0], args[1])\n                                shouldUseUnsignedComparison -> icmpULe(args[0], args[1])\n                                else -> icmpLe(args[0], args[1])\n                            }\n                        }\n                        functionSymbol == context.irBuiltIns.illegalArgumentExceptionSymbol -> {\n                            callDirect(\n                                    context.symbols.throwIllegalArgumentExceptionWithMessage.owner,\n                                    args,\n                                    Lifetime.GLOBAL,\n                                    null\n                            )\n                        }\n                        else -> TODO(function.name.toString())\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n\n    fun callDirect(function: IrSimpleFunction, args: List<LLVMValueRef>, resultLifetime: Lifetime, resultSlot: LLVMValueRef?): LLVMValueRef {\n        val functionDeclarations = codegen.getLlvmFunctionFrom(function.target)\n        return call(function, functionDeclarations, args, resultLifetime, resultSlot)\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n\n    fun callVirtual(function: IrSimpleFunction, args: List<LLVMValueRef>, resultLifetime: Lifetime, resultSlot: LLVMValueRef?): LLVMValueRef {\n        val functionDeclarations = codegen.getVirtualFunctionTrampoline(function)\n        return call(function, functionDeclarations, args, resultLifetime, resultSlot)\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n\n    private val IrSimpleFunction.needsNativeThreadState: Boolean\n        get() {\n            // We assume that call site thread state switching is required for interop calls only.\n            if (origin == CBridgeOrigin.KOTLIN_TO_C_BRIDGE) {\n                check(isExternal)\n                check(!annotations.hasAnnotation(KonanFqNames.gcUnsafeCall))\n                check(annotations.hasAnnotation(RuntimeNames.filterExceptions))\n                return true\n            }\n            if (annotations.hasAnnotation(RuntimeNames.importedBridge)) {\n                check(isExternal)\n                return true\n            }\n            return false\n        }\n\n    private fun call(function: IrSimpleFunction, llvmCallable: LlvmCallable, args: List<LLVMValueRef>,\n                     resultLifetime: Lifetime, resultSlot: LLVMValueRef?): LLVMValueRef {\n        check(!function.isTypedIntrinsic)\n\n        val foreignExceptionModeFromAnnotation = function.annotations.findAnnotation(RuntimeNames.filterExceptions)?.let {\n            ForeignExceptionMode.byValue(it.getConstArgument(\"mode\"))\n        }\n\n        val needsNativeThreadState: Boolean\n        val filterExceptionWith: ForeignExceptionMode.Mode?\n\n        val forceNativeThreadState = llvmCallable.name in context.config.forceNativeThreadStateForFunctions\n                || function.annotations.hasAnnotation(RuntimeNames.forceNativeThreadStateAnnotation)\n\n        if (forceNativeThreadState) {\n            // This is a quick hack for functions that break the contract of `SymbolName` by being blocking,\n            // and therefore need the native thread state.\n            // See e.g., KT-75895 and KT-79384.\n            needsNativeThreadState = true\n\n            // Switching to the native thread state requires a filteringExceptionHandler,\n            // so we enforce one here.\n            // Otherwise, nothing will switch the state back to runnable in case of exception.\n            // A more flexible approach can be implemented but is not necessary for this quick hack.\n            filterExceptionWith = foreignExceptionModeFromAnnotation ?: ForeignExceptionMode.Mode.TERMINATE\n        } else {\n            needsNativeThreadState = function.needsNativeThreadState\n            filterExceptionWith = foreignExceptionModeFromAnnotation\n                    ?: (needsNativeThreadState && function.annotations.hasAnnotation(RuntimeNames.importedBridge))\n                            .ifTrue { ForeignExceptionMode.Mode.TERMINATE }\n        }\n\n        val exceptionHandler = if (filterExceptionWith != null) {\n            functionGenerationContext.filteringExceptionHandler(\n                    currentCodeContext.exceptionHandler,\n                    filterExceptionWith,\n                    needsNativeThreadState\n            )\n        } else {\n            check(!needsNativeThreadState) {\n                \"${llvmCallable.name} needs native thread state, but doesn't have a filtering exception handler\"\n            }\n            currentCodeContext.exceptionHandler\n        }\n\n        if (needsNativeThreadState) {\n            functionGenerationContext.switchThreadState(ThreadState.Native)\n        }\n\n        val result = call(llvmCallable, args, resultLifetime, exceptionHandler, resultSlot)\n\n        when  {\n            function.returnType.isNothing() -> functionGenerationContext.unreachable()\n            needsNativeThreadState -> functionGenerationContext.switchThreadState(ThreadState.Runnable)\n        }\n\n        if (llvmCallable.returnType == llvm.voidType) {\n            return codegen.theUnitInstanceRef.llvm\n        }\n\n        return result\n    }\n\n    private fun call(\n            function: LlvmCallable, args: List<LLVMValueRef>,\n            resultLifetime: Lifetime = Lifetime.IRRELEVANT,\n            exceptionHandler: ExceptionHandler = currentCodeContext.exceptionHandler,\n            resultSlot: LLVMValueRef? = null\n    ): LLVMValueRef {\n        return functionGenerationContext.call(function, args, resultLifetime, exceptionHandler, resultSlot = resultSlot)\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n\n    private fun appendLlvmUsed(name: String, args: List<LLVMValueRef>) {\n        if (args.isEmpty()) return\n\n        LLVMSetSection(llvmUsedGlobal.llvmGlobal, \"llvm.metadata\")\n    }\n\n    // Globals set this way cannot be const, but are overridable when producing final executable.\n    private fun //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n    // Create type { i32, void ()*, i8* }\n\n    val kCtorType = llvm.structType(llvm.int32Type, llvm.pointerType, llvm.pointerType)\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n    // Create object { i32, void ()*, i8* } { i32 1, void ()* @ctorFunction, i8* null }\n\n    fun createGlobalCtor(ctorFunction: LlvmCallable): ConstPointer {\n        val priority = if (context.config.target.family == Family.MINGW) {\n            // Workaround MinGW bug. Using this value makes the compiler generate\n            // '.ctors' section instead of '.ctors.XXXXX', which can't be recognized by ld\n            // when string table is too long.\n            // More details: https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-39548\n            llvm.int32(65535)\n            // Note: this difference in priorities doesn't actually make initializers\n            // platform-dependent, because handling priorities for initializers\n            // from different object files is platform-dependent anyway.\n        } else {\n            llvm.kImmInt32One\n        }\n        val data = llvm.kNull\n        val argList = cValuesOf(priority, ctorFunction.toConstPointer().llvm, data)\n        val ctorItem = LLVMConstNamedStruct(kCtorType, argList, 3)!!\n        return constPointer(ctorItem)\n    }\n\n    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------//\n    fun appendStaticInitializers() {\n        // Note: the list of libraries is topologically sorted (in order for initializers to be called correctly).\n        val dependencies = (generationState.dependenciesTracker.allBitcodeDependencies + listOf(null)/* Null for \"current\" non-library module */)\n\n        val libraryToInitializers = dependencies.associate { it?.library to mutableListOf<RuntimeInitializer>() }\n\n        llvm.irStaticInitializers.forEach {\n            val library = it.konanLibrary\n            val initializers = libraryToInitializers[library]\n                    ?: error(\"initializer for not included library ${library?.path}\")\n\n            initializers.add(it.runtimeInitializer)\n        }\n\n        fun fileCtorName(libraryName: String, fileName: String) = \"$libraryName:$fileName\".moduleConstructorName\n\n        fun ctorProto(ctorName: String): LlvmFunctionProto {\n            return ctorFunctionSignature.toProto(ctorName, null, LLVMLinkage.LLVMExternalLinkage)\n        }\n\n        val ctorFunctions = dependencies.flatMap { dependency ->\n            val library = dependency?.library\n            val initializer = mergeRuntimeInitializers(libraryToInitializers.getValue(library))\n                    ?.let { createInitCtor(createInitNode(it)) }\n\n            val ctorName = when {\n                // TODO: Try to not use moduleId.\n                library == null -> (if (context.config.produce.isCache) generationState.outputFiles.cacheFileName else context.config.moduleId).moduleConstructorName\n                library == context.config.libraryToCache?.klib\n                        && context.config.producePerFileCache ->\n                    fileCtorName(library.uniqueName, generationState.outputFiles.perFileCacheFileName)\n                else -> library.moduleConstructorName\n            }\n\n            if (library == null || generationState.llvmModuleSpecification.containsLibrary(library)) {\n                val otherInitializers = llvm.otherStaticInitializers.takeIf { library == null }.orEmpty()\n\n                listOf(\n                    appendStaticInitializers(ctorProto(ctorName), listOfNotNull(initializer) + otherInitializers)\n                )\n            } else {\n                // A cached library.\n                check(initializer == null) {\n                    \"found initializer from ${library.path}, which is not included into compilation\"\n                }\n\n                val cache = context.config.cachedLibraries.getLibraryCache(library)\n                        ?: error(\"Library ${library.path} is expected to be cached\")\n\n                when (cache) {\n                    is CachedLibraries.Cache.Monolithic -> listOf(ctorProto(ctorName))\n /**
 * A collection that holds pairs of objects (keys and values) and supports retrieving
 * the value corresponding to each key, as well as adding new, removing or updating existing pairs.
 *
 * Map keys are unique; the map holds only one value for each key. In contrast, the same value can be associated with several unique keys.
 *
 * If a particular use case does not require map's modification, a read-only counterpart, \ref Map could be used instead.
 *
 * \ref MutableMap extends \ref Map contact with functions allowing to add, remove and update mapping between keys and values.
 *
 * Unlike \ref Map, \ref keys, \ref values and \ref entries collections are all mutable, and changes in them update the map.
 *
 * Until stated otherwise, \ref MutableMap implementations are not thread-safe and their modification without
 * explicit synchronization may result in data corruption, loss, and runtime errors.
 *
 * @param k the type of map keys. The map is invariant in its key type.
 * @param v the type of map values. The mutable map is invariant in its value type.
 */

 * to other suspend function, or, for a Unit-returning function, a call to other suspend function, also returning Unit.

/**
 * A generic ordered collection of elements that supports adding, replacing and removing elements, as well as
 * iterating over contained elements, accessing them by an index and checking if a collection contains a particular value.
 *
 * If a particular use case does not require list's modification,
 * a read-only counterpart, \ref List could be used instead.
 *
 * \ref MutableList extends \ref List contract with functions allowing to add, replace and remove elements.
 *
 * Unlike \ref List, iterators returned by \ref iterator and \ref list_iterator allow modifying the list during iteration.
 * A view returned by \ref sub_list also allows modifications of the underlying list.
 *
 * Until stated otherwise, \ref MutableList implementations are not thread-safe and their modification without
 * explicit synchronization may result in data corruption, loss, and runtime errors.
 *
 * @param e the type of elements contained in the list. The mutable list is invariant in its element type.
 */

 * Checks if the two specified arrays are *deeply* equal to one another.
 * 
 * Two arrays are considered deeply equal if they have the same size, and elements at corresponding indices are deeply equal.
 * That is, if two corresponding elements are nested arrays, they are also compared deeply.

 * Two arrays are considered structurally equal if they have the same size, and elements at corresponding indices are equal.

 * Two arrays are considered structurally equal if they have the same size, and elements at corresponding indices are equal.
 * Elements are compared for equality using the \ref Any::equals "equals" function.

__ast_distance_unmapped__("property_declaration", "var IrClass.declarationsAtFunctionReferenceLowering: List<IrDeclaration>? by irAttribute(copyByDefault = true)")
/**
 * This lowering transforms \ref IrRichFunctionReference nodes to an anonymous class.
 *
 * The class would have:
 *   * Constructor capturing all values from \ref IrRichFunctionReference::bound_values, and storing them to fields
 *   * A method overriding \ref IrRichFunctionReference::overridden_function_symbol, with body moved from \ref IrRichFunctionReference::invoke_function
 *   * \ref IrRichFunctionReference::type as a super-interface type (typically `[K][Suspend]FunctionN`,
 *     or fun interface the reference was sam converted to)
 *
 * Platforms can customize:
 *   * Super-class with platform-specific reference implementation details by overriding \ref get_super_class_type method
 *   * Equality/hashCode/toString and other reflection methods implementation by adding methods in overridden \ref generate_extra_methods method
 *   * exact names/origins of generated classes/methods by overriding corresponding methods
 *
 * For example, the following code:
 * ```kotlin
 * fun foo1(l: () -> String): String {
 *   return l()
 * }
 * fun <FooTP> foo2(v: FooTP, l: (FooTP) -> String): String {
 *   return l(v)
 * }
 *
 * private fun <T> bar(t: T): String { /* ... */ }
 *
 * fun <BarTP> bar(v: BarTP): String {
 *   return foo1(v::bar/*<T=BarTP>*/) + foo2(v) { bar/*<T=BarTP>*/(it) }
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * is lowered into:
 * ```kotlin
 * fun <BarTP> bar(v: BarTP): String {
 *   /*local*/ class <local-platform-specific-name-1>(p$0: BarTP) : KFunction0<String>, PlatformSpecificSuperType() {
 *     private val f$0: BarTP = p$0
 *     override fun invoke() = bar<BarTP>(f$0)
 *     // some platform specific reflection information
 *   }
 *   /*local*/ class <local-platform-specific-name-2> : Function1<BarTP, String>, PlatformSpecificSuperTypeProbablyAny() {
 *     override fun invoke(p0: BarTP) = bar<BarTP>(p0)
 *   }
 *   return foo1(<local-platform-specific-name-1>(v)) + foo2(v, <local-platform-specific-name-2>())
 * }
 * ```
 *
 * Note that as all these classes are defined as local ones, they don't need to explicitly capture local variables or any type parameters.
 * But it can happen, that \ref LocalDeclarationsLowering would later capture something additional into the classes.
 */
__ast_distance_unmapped__("class_declaration", "abstract class AbstractFunctionReferenceLowering<C : CommonBackendContext>(val context: C) : FileLoweringPass {\n    override fun lower(irFile: IrFile) {\n        irFile.transform(object : IrTransformer<IrDeclaration?>() {\n            override fun visitClass(declaration: IrClass, data: IrDeclaration?): IrStatement {\n                if (declaration.isFun || declaration.symbol.isKFunction() || declaration.symbol.isSuspendFunction() || declaration.symbol.isKSuspendFunction()) {\n                    declaration.declarationsAtFunctionReferenceLowering = declaration.declarations.toList()\n                }\n                declaration.transformChildren(this, declaration)\n                return declaration\n            }\n\n            override fun visitBody(body: IrBody, data: IrDeclaration?): IrBody {\n                return data!!.factory.stageController.restrictTo(data) {\n                    super.visitBody(body, data)\n                }\n            }\n\n            override fun visitDeclaration(declaration: IrDeclarationBase, data: IrDeclaration?): IrStatement {\n                declaration.transformChildren(this, declaration)\n                return declaration\n            }\n\n            override fun visitRichFunctionReference(expression: IrRichFunctionReference, data: /**
 * A generic collection of elements that supports iterating, adding and removing elements, as well as checking if the
 * collection contains some elements. Complex operations are built upon this
 * functionality and provided in form of \ref kotlin::collections extension functions.
 *
 * If a particular use case does not require collection's modification,
 * a read-only counterpart, \ref Collection could be used instead.
 *
 * \ref MutableCollection extends \ref Collection contract with functions allowing to add or remove elements.
 *
 * \ref MutableCollection is a top-level interface for mutable objects aggregating multiple different homogenous elements.
 * Other more specific interfaces, like \ref MutableList, \ref MutableSet, and \ref MutableMap extend \ref MutableCollection to provide
 * more specific guarantees on how elements are stored, accessed and modified, as well as provide richer functionality.
 *
 * Unlike \ref Collection, an iterator returned by \ref iterator allows removing elements during iteration.
 *
 * Until stated otherwise, \ref MutableCollection implementations are not thread-safe and their modification without
 * explicit synchronization may result in data corruption, loss, and runtime errors.
 *
 * @param e the type of elements contained in the collection. The mutable collection is invariant in its element type.
 */

/**
 * A special object that can be used to refer to \ref IrDeclarations and some other entities from IR nodes.
 *
 * For example, \ref IrCall uses \ref IrSimpleFunctionSymbol to refer to the \ref IrSimpleFunction that is being called.
 *
 * **Q:** Why not just use the \ref IrSimpleFunction class itself?
 *
 * **A:** Because a symbol, unlike a declaration, can be bound or unbound (see \ref is_bound).
 *
 * We need this distinction to work with IR before the linkage phase. In pre-linkage IR the symbols referencing declarations from
 * other modules are not yet bound.
 *
 * During the linkage phase, we collect all the unbound symbols in the IR tree and try to resolve them to the declarations they should
 * refer to. For unbound symbols for public declarations from other modules, \ref signature is used to resolve those declarations.
 *
 * @see IdSignature
 * @see SymbolTable
 */

Declaring this property nullable would make working with it more difficult most of the time.\n     */\n    @UnsafeDuringIrConstructionAPI\n    val owner: IrSymbolOwner\n\n    /**\n     * If [hasDescriptor] is `true`, returns the [DeclarationDescriptor] of the declaration that this symbol was created for.\n     * Otherwise, returns a dummy [IrBasedDeclarationDescriptor] that serves as a descriptor-like view to [owner].\n     */\n    @ObsoleteDescriptorBasedAPI\n    val descriptor: DeclarationDescriptor\n\n    /**\n     * Returns `true` if this symbol was created from a [DeclarationDescriptor] either emitted by the K1 (aka classic) frontend,\n     * or from deserialized metadata.\n     *\n     * @see descriptor\n     */\n    @ObsoleteDescriptorBasedAPI\n    val hasDescriptor: Boolean\n\n    /**\n     * Whether this symbol has already been resolved to its [owner].\n     */\n    val isBound: Boolean\n\n    /**\n     * If this symbol refers to a publicly accessible declaration (from the binary artifact point of view),\n     * returns the binary signature of that declaration.\n     *\n     * Otherwise, returns `null`.\n     *\n     * @see IdSignature.isPubliclyVisible\n     */\n    val signature: IdSignature?\n\n    // TODO: remove once JS IR IC migrates to a different stable tag generation scheme\n    // Used to store signatures in private symbols for JS IC\n    /**\n     * If this symbol refers to a local declaration, the signature of that declaration, otherwise `null`.\n     *\n     * @see IdSignature.isPubliclyVisible\n     */\n    var privateSignature: IdSignature?\n}")

/**
 * Transforms a mutable list in place.
 * Each element `it` is replaced with a result of `transformation(it)`,
 * `null` means "keep existing element" (to avoid creating excessive singleton lists).
 */
__ast_distance_unmapped__("function_declaration", "inline fun <T> MutableList<T>.transformFlat(transformation: (T) -> List<T>?) {\n    var i = 0\n    while (i < size) {\n        val item = get(i)\n\n        i = replaceInPlace(transformation(item), i)\n    }\n}")
/**
 * Transforms a subset of a mutable list in place.
 * Each element `it` that has a type S is replaced with a result of `transformation(it)`,
 * `null` means "keep existing element" (to avoid creating excessive singleton lists).
 */
__ast_distance_unmapped__("function_declaration", "inline fun <T, reified S : T> MutableList<T>.transformSubsetFlat(transformation: (S) -> List<S>?) {\n    var i = 0\n    while (i < size) {\n        val item = get(i)\n\n        if (item !is S) {\n            i++\n            continue\n        }\n\n        i = replaceInPlace(transformation(item), i)\n    }\n}")
__ast_distance_unmapped__("function_declaration", "@PublishedApi internal fun <T> MutableList<T>.replaceInPlace(transformed: List<T>?, atIndex: Int): Int {\n    var i = atIndex\n    when (transformed?.size) {\n        null -> i++\n        0 -> removeAt(i)\n        1 -> set(i++, transformed[0])\n        else -> {\n            addAll(i, transformed)\n            i += transformed.size\n            removeAt(i)\n        }\n    }\n    return i\n}")

__ast_distance_unmapped__("function_declaration", "fun <T : IrElement, D> List<T>.transformIfNeeded(transformer: IrTransformer<D>, data: D): List<T> {\n    var result: ArrayList<T>? = null\n    for ([i, item] in withIndex()) {\n        @Suppress(\"UNCHECKED_CAST\")\n        val transformed = item.transform(transformer, data) as T\n        if (transformed !== item && result == null) {\n            result = ArrayList(this)\n        }\n        result?.set(i, transformed)\n    }\n    return result ?: this\n}")
